judgments.rationale: Owl-carousel 'previous' button of the Hcor explica carousel (class owl-prev disabled: clicking it does nothing at the first slide, but it stays focusable and looks active). On the live page (headless Edge, 1280x800) the only change on keyboard focus is transform: scale(1.08); outline stays none and no colour changes. The reported indicator, #e9f2ec next to #e9f2ec at 1.00:1, is an artefact. Those are pixels inside the button that changed only because the arrow glyph moved when it scaled, not an indicator. Measured properly, the enlarged pale band is #e9f2ec on white (about 1.14:1) and the arrow is #64b483 on #e9f2ec (2.19:1). The button is also functionally inactive, and 1.4.11 exempts inactive components. Whether a size change alone is a focus indicator that 1.4.11 measures is contested: the Understanding document says 1.4.11 does not directly compare the focused and unfocused states of a control, while a strict reading treats the enlarged band as an indicator outside the component that must reach 3:1 with the background. Competent auditors would disagree, so neither label is safe.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: Header menu item 'Agendamentos' (the <li>, whose :hover opens the submenu of 13 links, 440x373 px). On the live page (1280x800), hovering the trigger sets the submenu <ul> to display:flex, absolutely positioned over the page content below the header. Pressing Escape with the pointer still on the trigger leaves it shown. The page has no Escape handler for the menu, and the only key handler in the theme scripts closes the mobile side nav. It is CSS hover only (focus does not open it), and the only way to close it is to move the pointer away. The Understanding document for 1.4.13 lists sub-menus explicitly. The content obscures other content and is not an error message, so the dismissible exception does not apply.

The link lands at y 164-190, under the mobile header (about y 0-282). Every grid point inside the focused element hit the header's opaque children, so the element is entirely hidden. This is the sticky-header failure F110. The banner is not content the user opened, so the Understanding note about content opened by the user does not apply. The probe's 'painting/hiding changed 0 px' comes from the header element itself having 0 px height and does not undo the geometry.
